newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran plans to become major gas exporter.
newsitem.headline: Iran plans to become major gas exporter.

text.p: Iran aims to export an annual 4.5 billion cubic metres (159 billion cubic feet) of gas at the end of the decade and has plans to increase this tenfold by the year 2005, a senior Iranian gas official said on Sunday.

In the year 2000 Iran would be exporting three billion cubic metres to Turkey, one billion to Armenia and 0.5 billion to Azerbaijan's Nakhichevan enclave, Reza Rostami Sani, Director of International Affairs at the National Iranian Gas Company (NIGC), told reporters.
Iran does not currently export gas in commercial quantities despite having the world's largest natural gas reserves after Russia.
NIGC's plans involve the export of 41.5 billion cum a year in 2005 through costly gas pipeline projects to Pakistan and Europe and liquefied natural gas (LNG) exports to the Far East.
These longer-term projects would need at least $16.5 billion in hard currency investment just in construction costs.
"Foreign participation is definitely required. These finances cannot come from local sources alone," Sani said at a gas conference on Iran's Kish Island in the Gulf.
Plans to export gas by pipeline to Pakistan involve the sale of between eight billion cum and 16 billion cum of Iranian gas starting in 2002.

The LNG scheme to the Far East would involve the sale of six million tonnes a year starting in 2002 while plans to export natural gas to Europe involve the sale of between eight and 32 billion cum a year starting in 2005.
Industry analysts have raised doubts about the economics of a pipeline running to Europe and the Pakistan plan is only at the feasibility study stage.
Work on laying a pipeline to connect Iran's gas network with that of neighbouring Turkey is expected to start next month for first deliveries at the end of 1998.
Tehran and Ankara signed a $23 billion, 23-year gas supply contract last year.
